versions.research_rationale: EO 11812 (Oct. 7, 1974, 'shall take effect October 1, 1974'; 39 FR 36307-36312) adjusts for members of the uniformed services the monthly basic pay (Sec. 1 tables), basic allowance for subsistence (Sec. 2) and basic allowance for quarters (Sec. 3), caps basic pay at Executive Schedule level V under 5 U.S.C. 5308 (Sec. 4), supersedes seven earlier uniformed-pay orders (Sec. 5) and sets its effective date (Sec. 6). It has no term of its own; its rates govern until the next adjustment. EO 11883 (signed Oct. 6, 1975) sec. 5 supersedes 'Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974', and its sec. 2 replacement rates for basic pay, subsistence and quarters 'shall be effective on October 1, 1975' (sec. 4). Every clause except Sec. 5 therefore first ended on 1975-10-01, the stated effective date in the acting instrument (the displacement was retroactive from that date to Oct. 6). Sec. 5's supersession of earlier orders was completed when the order issued on 1974-10-07 (spent). Whole-order end = 1975-10-01. All of this order concerns the uniformed services, so the agency-specific civilian pay-period dates in EO 11883 sec. 4 do not affect it. Counterevidence: the U.S. Code note under 37 U.S.C. 1009 states that EO 11812 'which provided for the adjustment of pay rates effective Oct. 1, 1974, was superseded by Ex. Ord. No. 11883' (history, not a predicate); the 1989 Codification row reads 'Superseded by EO 11883'. CONFLICT QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT resolved: the quarantined relationship (research/stage15/AUDIT/RELATIONSHIP_CHRONOLOGY_VIOLATIONS.csv) is an OFR note on EO 11778 (Apr. 12, 1974) reading 'Amends: EO 11692, December 15, 1972 (which was revoked by EO 11812, October 7, 1974)'; the parenthetical names this order as the later superseder of EO 11692, it is not an event on this order, and the Stage 15 audit already suppressed it. The draft had no clause inventory; it is built here from the official FR scan.
